input: File all loose receipts before the end of quarter

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this covers personal receipts, business expenses, or both determines the volume and categories involved, and whether tax/reimbursement rules apply.
Whether the user is filing for themselves alone, or also collecting receipts from a team/partner, changes coordination steps and who needs to be chased.
The physical vs. digital nature of the receipts determines the tools and workflow needed — scanning, photographing, or simply sorting existing digital files.
Knowing the exact end-of-quarter deadline and how many receipts are backlogged sets urgency and how much time to allocate per session.
Whether a filing system already exists (folder structure, expense app, spreadsheet) determines if setup work is needed before any filing can start.
The user may want receipts sorted by date, vendor, category, or project — the chosen schema shapes every filing decision downstream.
The end state could mean receipts submitted for reimbursement, reconciled against a bank statement, stored for audit, or simply not scattered on a desk — this defines what 'done' really means.

gold.taskTitle: File all loose receipts before end of quarter
gold.taskDescription: Organise and file every unfiled receipt before the current quarter closes.

questions.title: Are these receipts personal, business, or both?
questions.description: Establish whether the receipts relate to personal spending, business expenses, or a mix — this determines categories, rules, and filing complexity.

questions.title: Are you filing for yourself or also others?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is a solo task or involves collecting and chasing receipts from teammates, a partner, or direct reports.

questions.title: Are the receipts physical, digital, or a mix?
questions.description: Determine the format of the receipts so the right capture method (scanning, photographing, sorting files) can be planned.

questions.title: Roughly how many unfiled receipts are there?
questions.description: Gauge the volume of backlog to set realistic time estimates and decide whether this is a single session or a multi-day effort.

questions.title: Does a filing system already exist for receipts?
questions.description: Find out if there is an existing folder structure, expense app, or spreadsheet in place, or whether one needs to be created first.

questions.title: How do you want receipts organised once filed?
questions.description: Establish the preferred sorting schema — by date, vendor, expense category, project, or another method — to ensure consistent filing.

questions.title: What does fully done look like for this task?
questions.description: Define the finish line — receipts submitted for reimbursement, reconciled against statements, archived for audit, or simply off the desk.
